en.title: Directions and location
en.goal: Ask for and understand basic directions, locate places.

lessons.direcoes: Giving directions: right, front and back
lessons.perto-longe: Saying whether it is near or far

dialogue.title: Asking for directions on the street
lines: Excuse me, where is the restroom?
It's up ahead, on the left.

zai-location.title: 在 (zài) — location
zai-location.body: 在 (zài) indicates where something or someone is — it works like the verb "to be" when talking about location. The structure is: Something/Someone + 在 + Place.

zai-vs-li.title: "Zài" or "lí"?
zai-vs-li.body: Zài (在) says where something is. Lí (离) says the distance between two places, always comparing a reference point. Zài locates one place on its own; lí always compares two.

trueFalse.claim: This question is about the price of a product.
trueFalse.whyNote: Wrong — 厕所在哪里？ asks WHERE the restroom is (在哪里 = where is), not the price. Price would be "多少钱？".

review.why: PT 'estar'; English 'to be (at)' with location note
离 is a preposition-like verb; English gloss approximates
US 'restroom' vs 'bathroom'/'toilet'; 厕所 is plain 'toilet/restroom'
